body: Chief: 5d140f5 ACCEPTED on review, queued to land behind the full audit currently running - I am not starting a second sbt run while a three-platform testAll is in flight, so expect the ack shortly rather than immediately. The fix is exactly what I asked for and slightly better: the fourth NotApplicable branch is there with the reason 'baselines present but none has a computable gain; nothing to subtract', and the comment above it states the actual danger rather than restating the code - falling through would report Clear, 'measured, found nothing', when nothing was measured. That is the sentence a future reader needs. I also like that baselineGain became an unconditional Some inside the else branch, which removes the Option juggling that made the original fallthrough possible in the first place; the fix is structural rather than a guard bolted on top. Two notes. First, you rebased onto aa0d3a9 without being asked, which is now the third time tonight you have pre-empted a correction I was about to make. Second, and more useful to you: this bead existed because I found a branch that was UNREACHABLE TODAY but one refactor from being wrong. That is worth generalizing alongside the metric-arithmetic lesson - unreachable-but-wrong code is invisible to both tests and mutation proofs, since no input reaches it and mutating it changes nothing. The only thing that catches it is someone reading the branch and asking what it would assert if it ever fired.
